name: Tatiana Santo Domingo
current_role: Co-founder and creative director, Muzungu Sisters (ethical fashion brand)
profile: Born 1983 in New York and raised in Geneva and Paris, she is a granddaughter of Colombian magnate Julio Mario Santo Domingo, whose Bavaria brewery fortune passed into SABMiller; she inherited a share on his 2011 death. She co-founded the ethical slow-fashion label Muzungu Sisters with Dana Alikhani (launched 2011) and is married to Andrea Casiraghi of Monaco.
interesting_fact: Muzungu Sisters works with around 41 artisan communities worldwide; 'muzungu' is a Swahili word for wanderer/traveller.
deep_cut_fact: She studied photography and visual communications at the American University in London, and before Muzungu Sisters worked at AEFFE in New York, for art director Giovanni Bianco (GB65) and at Vanity Fair.
notes: Also known as Tatiana Casiraghi (Monaco royal family by marriage); very private. Business link is fashion, not energy; best route is via Muzungu Sisters general contact.

name: Ilona Herlin
current_role: Chair of the Board, Kone Foundation (2026–); Docent in Finnish language, University of Helsinki; major Cargotec shareholder (via Pivosto Oy)
profile: Daughter of Kone chief Pekka Herlin and great-granddaughter of Harald Herlin, who invested in Kone in 1924. After the 2005 Kone/Cargotec demerger she and her brothers became leading owners of Cargotec (cargo-handling machinery). She is an academic linguist and long-time board member of the Kone Foundation, a major Finnish arts and science funder, which she now chairs.
interesting_fact: She is a working linguist (PhD, University of Helsinki) whose research has prompted debate about simplifying Finnish; she still publishes, e.g. a 2025 Virittäjä article on 'responsibility for language, responsibility for nature'.
deep_cut_fact: Her doctoral dissertation was on Finnish subordinating conjunctions, and in the 2010s she published a study of the much-debated 'alkaa tekemään' construction (using the 3rd infinitive after 'alkaa').
notes: Low-profile; academic email is published (obfuscated) on the University of Helsinki research portal. Kone Foundation chair since 2026, on its board since 1995. Also listed on board of an electrosensitivity foundation per fi.wikipedia.

name: Zhou Xiaoguang
current_role: Founder/former chairman, Neoglory Holdings Group (新光控股集团), Zhejiang — group in bankruptcy restructuring since 2019
profile: Born 1962 in Zhuji, Zhejiang, Zhou built Neoglory from a jewellery/ornament trading business in Yiwu into a conglomerate with large real estate holdings, and was a National People's Congress deputy (10th and 11th NPC). Neoglory defaulted on bonds in 2018 and entered bankruptcy proceedings in 2019; she no longer appears on rich lists after 2018.
interesting_fact: In 2018, shortly before its debt crisis, Neoglory sought to spend over RMB 8bn acquiring Hong Kong-listed China High Speed Transmission, a wind-turbine gearbox maker, to enter the wind-power market.
deep_cut_fact: She started out at 17 as a street-stall vendor ("地摊妹") with no capital, a rags-to-riches story that made her a celebrated model entrepreneur in China; she later studied economic management at Zhejiang University.
notes: Sensitive: Neoglory's 2018 bond default and bankruptcy; in Dec 2019 regulators imposed a 10-year securities-market ban on her and her husband (wallstreetcn.com/articles/3519767, nbd.com.cn). No recent public activity found; not a good podcast prospect. No published contact found.

name: Hui Wing Mau
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, Shimao Group Holdings (HK:0813); chairman until Sept 2024, when son Jason Hui reportedly took over as chairman
profile: Hui Wing Mau (Xu Rongmao), born 1950 in Shishi, Fujian, founded Shimao, a Hong Kong-listed developer with projects across dozens of Chinese cities, and chaired it from 2004. Shimao defaulted on bonds in 2022 and has been restructuring its offshore debt; leadership has passed to his son Jason, with daughter Carol at Shanghai Shimao.
interesting_fact: Shimao's portfolio has long mixed residential development with hotels and landmark commercial towers; Hui describes 34+ years in property development, property investment and hotel operation.
deep_cut_fact: Before Shimao, Hui moved to Hong Kong in the 1980s, says he made his first fortune in the local stock market, lived for a time in Australia (he holds an MBA from the University of South Australia), then returned to invest in Shanghai and Beijing property.
notes: Also known as Xu Rongmao. Sensitive context: Shimao's 2022 defaults and ongoing debt restructuring; trading suspended into 2023. Chair handover per Webb-site officer records (webbsite.renavon.com) – verify. Very unlikely to do media; IR email is the only published route.

name: Raj Kumar Hiranandani
current_role: Founder/owner, Royal Holdings (now presented as RK Global family office), Singapore
profile: Indian-origin Singapore property magnate who formed Royal Holdings in 2011 when the family's Royal Brothers property business was divided with his brother Asok Kumar Hiranandani (Royal Group). Holdings span hotels, offices, retail and medical property, including riverside hotels at Clarke Quay and Robertson Quay. His son Kishin RK runs the affiliated RB Capital.
interesting_fact: A 2014 Wealth-X ranking placed him second among Singapore's richest property tycoons (US$1.4bn), with his brother seventh.
notes: Very low profile; little recent coverage of him personally (no evidence of death found, but nothing recent either). Son Kishin RK (RB Capital CEO, profiled by Tatler/The Peak) is the public face of the family and the more likely interviewee. RB Capital site cross-links RoyalHoldings.com.sg and lists the family office contact.

name: Michael Heine
current_role: Co-founder and non-executive director, Netwealth Group (ASX:NWL)
profile: Born c.1949, Heine worked with his father Walter in commodities, international financing, mortgage lending and property, started a fund-management business in 1982, and in 1999 founded wealth platform Netwealth with brother Leslie. Netwealth listed in 2017 and now has about A$100bn in funds under administration. He stepped down as joint MD in 2022; son Matt is MD and CEO.
interesting_fact: His father Walter fled Nazi Germany, was shipped to Australia as an 'enemy alien' aboard HMT Dunera, and in 1946 founded Heine Brothers, the family business Michael joined straight out of high school.
deep_cut_fact: In 1993 the Heine brothers' Heine Management bought 120 Collins Street in Melbourne, then Australia's tallest building, for A$286m.

public_contacts.value: Between Meetings with Matt Heine, Ep 100: 'Crafting a 25-year overnight success' (guest appearance)

notes: Rarely gives interviews, but did a long-form podcast with his son on Netwealth's own show (2025), so he is podcast-friendly in the right context. Best route is via Netwealth company secretary / shareholder email or through son Matt Heine.

name: Ranjit Singh Boparan
current_role: Founder and co-owner (with wife Baljinder) of Boparan Holdings / 2 Sisters Food Group; also behind Boparan Private Office (restaurant and other investments)
profile: Input name 'Ranjith' refers to Ranjit Singh Boparan (b. 1966, Bilston), the West Midlands 'Chicken King'. He left school at 16, worked in a butcher's shop, and in 1993 founded 2 Sisters Food Group with a small bank loan, growing it by acquisition (incl. Northern Foods, 2011) into the UK's biggest poultry supplier, providing about a third of UK supermarket chicken. He returned to run the poultry division in 2019.
interesting_fact: 2 Sisters began as a small frozen-retail cutting and packing operation in West Bromwich and became, by turnover, the UK's largest food manufacturer, with 20,000+ staff.
deep_cut_fact: A colleague quoted in 2019 on why he came back to hands-on management: "He loves the day to day. He is not about the next yacht or next fast car, he likes his chicken."
notes: Identity: 'Ranjith' = Ranjit Singh Boparan; shared fortune with wife Baljinder (spelled 'Beljinder' in input). Sensitive: 2017 Guardian/ITV food-standards investigation; avoid family topics. 2sfg.com blocked automated fetch so no published press email verified; try 2sfg.com media/contact page manually. Low media profile.

name: Gretel Packer
current_role: Chair, Packer Family Foundation; private investor; arts philanthropist (Art Gallery of NSW, Sydney Theatre Company Foundation)
profile: Daughter of media mogul Kerry Packer and elder sister of James Packer, she became a billionaire after the family fortune was divided in 2015, giving her investments including a Crown Resorts stake. Famously low-profile, she drove the creation of the A$160m National Philanthropic Fund (2014) and chairs the Packer Family Foundation, focusing on arts, education and environmental science.
interesting_fact: She was one of five women donors credited with championing the Art Gallery of NSW's Sydney Modern expansion, and served as vice-president of the gallery's board of trustees.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2020 she and the Packer Family Foundation pledged A$240,000 to a philanthropist-backed rescue of Sydney's Carriageworks arts centre when it went into administration during COVID.
notes: Very private; no published personal, office or foundation contact found. Avoid family-settlement topics. Only plausible route is via arts institutions she serves (AGNSW, Sydney Theatre Company Foundation). Appointed AM (2020) per Wikipedia. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so contacts not exhaustively checked.

name: Govindbhai Laljibhai Dholakia
current_role: Founder and chairman, Shree Ramkrishna Exports (SRK), Surat; Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha (BJP, Gujarat) since April 2024
profile: Born 1949 into a farming family in Dudhala, Amreli district, Gujarat, Dholakia moved to Surat in 1964 to work as a diamond polisher and went on to found Shree Ramkrishna Exports, one of India's largest diamond manufacturers/exporters. Known as 'Kaka', he entered the Rajya Sabha in 2024 and remains a prominent philanthropist.
interesting_fact: His autobiography 'Diamonds Are Forever, So Are Morals' (Penguin Random House, 2022) was co-written with Arun Tiwari, co-author of APJ Abdul Kalam's 'Wings of Fire'.
deep_cut_fact: Through SRK's CSR arm he funded the full solarisation of his home village Dudhala (2022), billed as Gujarat's first village completely solarised by a foundation; he also received a 2017 Leadership Award from the U.S. Green Building Council.
notes: Strong energy angle (solar village, green-building award). The email is the company contact listed in SRK's website footer (Mumbai BDB office), a staff address rather than his own. As a sitting MP, official contact details also appear on sansad.in. Hurun 2022 named SRK 'Most Respected Family Business'.

name: Lord Grantchester
current_role: Labour life peer, House of Lords (from 15 June 2026); dairy farmer near Crewe, Cheshire
profile: Christopher John Suenson-Taylor, 3rd Baron Grantchester (b. 1951; known as John Grantchester), is a grandson of Sir John Moores, founder of the Littlewoods retail and football-pools empire, and a former Littlewoods director. Educated at Winchester and the LSE (economics), he sat as an elected hereditary peer from 2003 and was made a life peer in 2026 after hereditary seats were abolished.
interesting_fact: He is a former Everton FC director and long-time shareholder (8.5% as of 2015), and a trustee of the Everton Collection, a large open-access archive of club memorabilia.
deep_cut_fact: A working dairy farmer, he runs a farm near Crewe, chairs the South West Cheshire Dairy Association and sits on the council of the Royal Agricultural Society of England; he has been a Labour frontbench voice on agriculture in the Lords.
notes: Rich-list entry is for the wider Moores family fortune. Parliamentary email is the clear published route. Note: he chaired Dairy Farmers of Britain when it collapsed in 2009 — avoid as an opener.

name: Margaret Cargill
profile: Margaret Anne Cargill (1920–2006), granddaughter of Cargill founder W. W. Cargill and heir to the grain-trading fortune, died on August 1, 2006 in La Jolla, California; her estate endowed Margaret A. Cargill Philanthropies.
notes: Deceased (d. 2006, per Wikipedia / LA Times obituary). Skipped further research.

name: Francisco Jose Riberas Mera
profile: Francisco José Riberas Mera and his brother Juan María each own about 25% of Gestamp, the autoparts maker he founded in 1997 from the family steel business started by their father in 1958; the family holds its stake via holding company ACEK. Gestamp makes body-in-white, chassis and battery-box components in 20+ countries and reported €11.3bn revenue in 2025. The brothers are also top shareholders in CIE Automotive.
interesting_fact: In March 2026 Gestamp signed a 10-year renewable-energy PPA with Iberdrola for 660,000 MWh of electricity for its European plants, and it supplies scrap via Gescrap to Hydnum Steel's green-hydrogen steelmaking.
deep_cut_fact: For Gestamp's 25th anniversary in 2023, Riberas personally guided King Felipe VI around the Palencia plant that makes structural bodywork and chassis parts.
notes: Good energy-transition angle (PPAs, green steel, EV battery boxes). Gestamp press office is the published route. Web search budget ran out before checking personal social accounts.

name: Xu Jingnan
current_role: Chairman, Peak Sport Products (匹克体育), Quanzhou, Fujian
profile: Xu Jingnan (许景南) is the founder and chairman of Peak Sport, a Quanzhou-based basketball-focused sportswear and footwear brand founded in 1989; he and his family held about 65% of the company when it was listed in Hong Kong (taken private in 2016). Peak now sells in about 110 countries, and his son Xu Zhihua is CEO.
interesting_fact: Peak built its brand on basketball, signing NBA players such as Tony Parker and Dwight Howard and sponsoring FIBA and the WTA; its in-house 'TAICHI' adaptive-cushioning shoe tech had sold over 40 million pairs by end-2022.
notes: Low international media profile; son Xu Zhihua (CEO) is the public face of Peak. No published press email for the chairman found (only a consumer customer-service address for the overseas webstore). Web search budget ran out before a deep-cut fact could be sourced.

name: Vladimir Evtushenkov
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder (~49%) of AFK Sistema; stepped down from Sistema's board in April 2022
profile: Vladimir Yevtushenkov (b. 1948, Smolensk), a chemical engineer by training, left Moscow city government in 1993 to build Sistema into a conglomerate spanning telecoms (MTS), banking, retail and other assets, taking it public in London in 2005 in a then-record $1.35bn Russian IPO. After UK and Australian sanctions in 2022 he cut his stake below 50% and left the board.
interesting_fact: Sistema's 2005 London IPO, at $1.35bn, was the largest ever by a Russian company at the time.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he trained as a chemist (Mendeleev Moscow Chemical Engineering Institute, 1973) and worked as an engineer at the Karacharovo Plastics Works, then as chief engineer of the Polymerbyt research-and-production association.
notes: Under UK (Apr 2022) and Australian sanctions — journalist should check legal/compliance implications before any engagement. Sistema websites are geo/WAF-blocked from here; no published contact retrieved. Not recommended as a podcast guest.

name: Jenny Lindén Urnes
current_role: Chair and owner, Lindéngruppen AB (Höganäs, Sweden)
profile: Born 1971, Lindén Urnes inherited Lindéngruppen from her father Ulf G. Lindén, an ex-Volvo executive who bought Beckers and built a stake in Höganäs AB. The family group now owns Beckers (coil and industrial coatings), Colart (Winsor & Newton, Liquitex), Alex Begg (cashmere) and parts of Höganäs (world's largest metal-powder maker) and oat-ingredient maker cReal; combined 2025 turnover was about SEK 19.5bn.
interesting_fact: Höganäs is the world's largest producer of metal powder (about a third of the global market), used in components and to remove contaminants from drinking water; in 2013 she and a Wallenberg-linked foundation took it private.
deep_cut_fact: She studied art history (BA, Heythrop College, University of London, 1995), chairs the Färgfabriken contemporary-art foundation in Stockholm, and in 2015 was made an honorary doctor of Lund University School of Economics and Management.
notes: Forbes says she majored in philosophy; Swedish Wikipedia says art history at Heythrop (a philosophy/theology college) — wording kept neutral. Group has a sustainability focus ('lead the transformation to a sustainable world'), a good podcast hook. Also breeds horses (Forbes).

name: Burhan Karim
current_role: Director, Musim Mas Holdings (Singapore-based integrated palm oil group)
profile: Burhan Karim (Lim Ek Kian) runs Musim Mas with his brothers Bachtiar and Bahari. Their late father Anwar founded the Nam Cheong Soap Factory in Medan in 1932; the family opened Indonesia's first palm oil refinery in 1970 and set up Musim Mas in 1972. The group now operates in 14 countries across plantations, refining, oleochemicals, biodiesel and consumer products.
interesting_fact: Musim Mas says it was the first major oil palm group to have all its Indonesian plantations with mills 100% RSPO-certified (2012) and the first palm oil major verified by the Palm Oil Innovation Group (2019); it also runs what it calls Indonesia's largest smallholder programme.
notes: Very private family; brother Bachtiar Karim is the more visible family member. Energy angle: Musim Mas makes biodiesel and has a net-zero commitment. No published press email found. Web search budget ran out before a personal deep-cut fact could be sourced.
